title: Delivery guarantees: at-least-once and the idempotency it forces

videos.script: Event Hubs delivers every event at least once. At least once means sometimes twice. {{twice}} The app sends a payment and the answer never comes back. It cannot know whether the payment arrived, so it sends it again. Now there are two. {{retry}} A reader adds a payment to a customer's total. Then it dies before writing its checkpoint. When it starts again, it adds that payment a second time. {{crash}} Nothing reports an error. The totals are simply wrong, and somebody sends them to finance. {{wrong}} In this lesson you will make that happen on purpose, against the emulator, with a reader that crashes halfway. {{demo}} Then you will fix it twice. Once by remembering the last sequence number handled, which cures the crash and not the retry. And once by writing each payment under its order id, which cures both. {{fixed}} Exactly once is never a setting you switch on. It is something the whole pipeline earns, end to end. {{end}}
